Optimize a pose graph

Source: R/pose-graph.R
pose_graph_optimize.Rd

Minimizes \(\sum e_{ij}^\top \Omega_{ij} e_{ij}\) over the node poses with Gauss-Newton iterations and Levenberg-Marquardt damping. For SE(2) graphs the residual is \(e_{ij} = (R_z^\top(R_i^\top(t_j - t_i) - t_z), \mathrm{wrap}(\theta_j - \theta_i - \theta_z))\), analytic Jacobians (Grisetti et al., 2010, "A tutorial on graph-based SLAM") and sparse linear algebra from 'Matrix', and headings are wrapped after each update. For SE(3) graphs the residual is \(e_{ij} = \log(Z_{ij}^{-1} X_i^{-1} X_j)\) (translation first), nodes are updated on the manifold as \(X \exp(\delta)\), and the Jacobians with respect to \(\delta\) are \(J_r(e)^{-1}\) and \(-J_r(e)^{-1} \mathrm{Ad}(X_j^{-1} X_i)\), taken in the chart of the residual returned by the logarithm so that they stay valid when a residual rotation is near \(\pi\). Node fixed is held constant to remove the gauge freedom; every node must be connected to it through edges.

Usage

pose_graph_optimize(graph, fixed = 1, max_iterations = 50, tol = 1e-12)

Arguments

graph

A robot_pose_graph.

fixed

Index of the anchored node.

max_iterations

Maximum iterations (0 only evaluates the graph).

tol

Relative cost decrease treated as no progress.

Value

A list with the optimized graph, cost history, iterations, converged (TRUE only for status == "converged"), status and gradient, the largest scaled gradient component at the start of the last iteration.

Details

Convergence means stationarity, not merely a small change: the optimizer stops with status = "converged" when every residual component is at roundoff level for the magnitudes involved, or every gradient component is negligible on its own scale (\(|g_k| \le 10^{-6} \sqrt{H_{kk}} \sqrt{c}\)). A very precise coordinate therefore cannot hide an error in another. A graph with a single node is returned unchanged as converged. Other outcomes are "stalled" (the relative decrease fell below tol, or no damped step decreased the cost, while the gradient is not negligible), "max_iterations", "linear_solve_failed" and "invalid_graph" (nodes not connected to fixed; the graph is returned unchanged with a warning). A noisy graph converges to a positive cost.

Examples

g <- robot_pose_graph(rbind(c(0, 0, 0), c(1.2, 0.1, 0.1), c(1.9, 1.2, 1.7)))
g <- pose_graph_add_edge(g, 1, 2, c(1, 0, pi / 2))
g <- pose_graph_add_edge(g, 2, 3, c(1, 0, pi / 2))
res <- pose_graph_optimize(g)
round(res$graph$nodes, 6)
#>      [,1] [,2]      [,3]
#> [1,]    0    0  0.000000
#> [2,]    1    0  1.570796
#> [3,]    1    1 -3.141593
